motivation: The pooled pre-loss local-history effect predicts Thalassia re-recording after one-year loss. Restrict to loss-year meter marks with no seagrass present to test whether the history signal persists without above-ground community continuity.

primary_population.base_sequence: same frozen three-year exact-point Thalassia-loss sequences as microsite_recovery_pathway_v1
primary_population.pre_loss_run_length: number of immediately consecutive consensus years ending in the source year with Thalassia recorded present at the same stable point; stop at first missing year or Thalassia-absent year; minimum=1

primary_hypothesis.statement: Among meter marks that become seagrass-bare after Thalassia loss, longer-than-usual pre-loss Thalassia persistence within the same stable transect is associated with higher one-year Thalassia re-recording.
primary_hypothesis.predictor: pre_loss_run_length centered by stable-node mean within the bare-loss subgroup
primary_hypothesis.outcome: Thalassia recorded present at the same meter mark in the recovery year
primary_hypothesis.support_rule: lower bound of 95% node-bootstrap interval for the centered run-length coefficient > 0

interpretation.supported: A focal-history signal persists even when above-ground seagrass occupancy is lost, strengthening a local legacy / residual below-ground structure / persistent microsite interpretation.
interpretation.unsupported: The focal-history signal does not remain robust in bare loss states; the broader legacy association may depend on community continuity or other state differences.

claim_boundary: Post-hoc subgroup analysis of an already-opened recovery endpoint.
A positive result would still not prove residual rhizomes or clonal memory; persistent substrate/habitat quality and detectability remain alternatives.
Return is recorded reappearance at the same meter mark, not genet-level recolonization.
Do not alter the bare-state definition, run-length definition, node-centering, control set, model, minima, or support threshold after opening the subgroup history result.
If frozen minima fail, retain non-estimable status rather than pooling vegetated loss states back in.
